plants.name: Tomatoes
plants.growthForm: branching upright or vining fruiting plant
plants.regionalContext: Temperate United States with New England planning emphasis; local climate and cultivar selection take precedence.

spacingInches.text: 18–24 in plants; 30–36 in rows in current guide

matureSizeInches.planningNote: Determinate and indeterminate cultivars differ greatly.

planting.directSow: Usually not recommended in short seasons.
planting.transplant: After frost when nights and soil are reliably warm.

plants.harvest: Harvest fully colored fruit at the desired ripeness stage; mature-green harvest is possible before frost.
plants.support: Stake, cage, or trellis indeterminate and many determinate types.
plants.pollination: Mostly self-pollinating; vibration by wind or bees improves fruit set.
notes: Integration separates the supplied 18–24 inch between-plant interval from the 30–36 inch row interval; original combined bounds are retained in suppliedSpacingInches.

suppliedSpacingInches.text: 18–24 in plants; 30–36 in rows in current guide

plants.name: Cucumbers
plants.regionalContext: Temperate United States with New England planning emphasis; local climate and cultivar selection take precedence.

spacingInches.text: 8–12 in after thinning; 12–18 in on trellis in current guide

matureSizeInches.planningNote: Vining types may occupy several feet; trellising reduces ground footprint.

planting.directSow: Preferred after frost when soil reaches about 70°F.
planting.transplant: Young transplants after frost; minimize root disturbance.

plants.harvest: Harvest frequently at cultivar-appropriate size before fruit becomes overmature.
plants.support: Trellis optional but useful for vining types.
plants.pollination: Separate male/female flowers; insect pollination is important.

plants.name: Peppers
plants.scientificName: Capsicum annuum (common garden types; other Capsicum spp. also grown)
plants.regionalContext: Temperate United States with New England planning emphasis; local climate and cultivar selection take precedence.

spacingInches.text: 18–24 in between plants

matureSizeInches.planningNote: Hot and sweet pepper cultivars range from compact to tall.

planting.directSow: Not recommended in most temperate gardens.
planting.transplant: After frost when nighttime lows are above about 50°F.

plants.harvest: Harvest green or allow fruit to reach mature cultivar color and flavor.
plants.pollination: Mostly self-pollinating; insect visitation can help.

plants.name: Beans
plants.regionalContext: Temperate United States with New England planning emphasis; local climate and cultivar selection take precedence.

spacingInches.text: Bush 4–6 in; pole 6–8 in with support

matureSizeInches.planningNote: Habit must be chosen at cultivar/placement level: bush beans are compact; pole beans can exceed 6 ft.

planting.directSow: Preferred after frost once soil is warm.
planting.transplant: Usually avoided because roots dislike disturbance.

plants.harvest: Harvest snap pods young and frequently; shell/dry beans remain longer to mature.
plants.support: Pole beans require a trellis/poles; bush beans do not.
plants.pollination: Common beans are primarily self-pollinating.

plants.name: Carrots
plants.regionalContext: Temperate United States with New England planning emphasis; local climate and cultivar selection take precedence.

spacingInches.text: Thin to about 2–4 in; current guide says 1–3 in depending on desired root size

matureSizeInches.planningNote: Generalized planning range; cultivar and management can materially change mature dimensions.

planting.directSow: Always direct seed; transplanting damages taproots.
planting.transplant: Not recommended.

plants.harvest: Pull roots when they reach cultivar size; fall carrots can sweeten in cool weather.

plants.name: Zucchini
plants.growthForm: bush-form summer squash with very large leaves
plants.regionalContext: Temperate United States with New England planning emphasis; local climate and cultivar selection take precedence.

spacingInches.text: 24–36 in between plants

matureSizeInches.planningNote: Generalized planning range; cultivar and management can materially change mature dimensions.

planting.directSow: After frost once soil is warm.
planting.transplant: Young transplants after frost; minimize root disturbance.

plants.harvest: Harvest young fruit frequently for best texture and continued production.
plants.pollination: Separate male and female flowers; insect pollination is important.

plants.name: Onions
plants.regionalContext: Temperate United States with New England planning emphasis; local climate and cultivar selection take precedence.

spacingInches.text: 3–4 in after thinning/transplanting; 4–6 in in current guide

matureSizeInches.planningNote: Generalized planning range; cultivar and management can materially change mature dimensions.

planting.directSow: As soon as soil is workable in spring.
planting.transplant: Early spring; sets or transplants tolerate light frost.

plants.harvest: Harvest bulbs when tops naturally fall and begin drying; cure before storage.

plants.name: Lettuce
plants.regionalContext: Temperate United States with New England planning emphasis; local climate and cultivar selection take precedence.

spacingInches.text: 6–12 in depending on harvest stage

matureSizeInches.planningNote: Generalized planning range; cultivar and management can materially change mature dimensions.

planting.directSow: As soon as soil can be worked; succession sow in cool weather.
planting.transplant: Early spring and late summer.

plants.harvest: Harvest baby leaves as cut-and-come-again or cut mature heads before bolting.

plants.name: Peas
plants.regionalContext: Temperate United States with New England planning emphasis; local climate and cultivar selection take precedence.

spacingInches.text: 2–3 in with support for taller varieties

matureSizeInches.planningNote: Tall vines may reach about 5 ft; bush types commonly 2–3 ft.

planting.directSow: Early spring as soon as soil can be worked.
planting.transplant: Usually unnecessary.

plants.harvest: Pick pods promptly at full edible size before peas become starchy.
plants.support: Trellis for tall cultivars; dwarf types may self-support.
plants.pollination: Primarily self-pollinating.

plants.name: Basil
plants.regionalContext: Temperate United States with New England planning emphasis; local climate and cultivar selection take precedence.

spacingInches.text: typically 8–18 in depending on cultivar

matureSizeInches.planningNote: Compact basil may stay under 1 ft; Thai and vigorous types can reach 2–3 ft.

timeToHarvest.text: harvest can begin well before full maturity

planting.directSow: After danger of frost.
planting.transplant: After frost and once soil is warm.

plants.harvest: Pinch/harvest stems regularly; harvest before heavy flowering for leaf production.
plants.pollination: Flowers attract bees when allowed to bloom.

plants.name: Potatoes
plants.regionalContext: Temperate United States with New England planning emphasis; local climate and cultivar selection take precedence.

spacingInches.text: 10–12 in between seed pieces

matureSizeInches.planningNote: Generalized planning range; cultivar and management can materially change mature dimensions.

planting.directSow: Plant certified seed-potato pieces in cool spring soil.
planting.transplant: Not applicable.

plants.harvest: Dig new potatoes after flowering; harvest main crop when vines senesce and skins set.

plants.name: Strawberries
plants.regionalContext: Temperate United States with New England planning emphasis; local climate and cultivar selection take precedence.
plants.frostTolerance: winter hardy by cultivar; flowers sensitive to late frost

spacingInches.text: 12–18 in basic spacing; 18–24 in common matted-row systems

matureSizeInches.planningNote: Runners can rapidly extend beyond the mother-plant footprint.

timeToHarvest.text: Day-neutral/everbearing plants may fruit first year; June-bearing systems usually emphasize establishment.

planting.directSow: Not used for named garden cultivars.
planting.transplant: Plant dormant or potted transplants in spring.

plants.harvest: Pick fully colored berries frequently; renovate June-bearing beds after harvest.
plants.pollination: Self-fertile but bees are important for complete pollination.

plants.name: Corn
plants.regionalContext: Temperate United States with New England planning emphasis; local climate and cultivar selection take precedence.

spacingInches.text: 8–12 in in blocks; 24–36 in between rows

matureSizeInches.planningNote: Generalized planning range; cultivar and management can materially change mature dimensions.

planting.directSow: After soil warms; plant in blocks for pollination.
planting.transplant: Usually not preferred.

plants.harvest: Harvest sweet corn when silks brown and kernels are full/milky; timing varies by type.
plants.pollination: Wind-pollinated; block planting improves kernel set.

plants.name: Spinach
plants.regionalContext: Temperate United States with New England planning emphasis; local climate and cultivar selection take precedence.

spacingInches.text: 4–6 in for mature plants

matureSizeInches.planningNote: Generalized planning range; cultivar and management can materially change mature dimensions.

planting.directSow: Early spring, late summer, or fall.
planting.transplant: Possible young but direct sowing is common.

plants.harvest: Harvest baby leaves or entire mature rosettes before bolting.

plants.name: Garlic
plants.regionalContext: Temperate United States with New England planning emphasis; local climate and cultivar selection take precedence.
plants.frostTolerance: winter hardy in many temperate climates

spacingInches.text: 4–6 in between cloves

matureSizeInches.planningNote: Generalized planning range; cultivar and management can materially change mature dimensions.

planting.directSow: Plant cloves in fall before ground freezes.
planting.transplant: Not applicable.

plants.harvest: Harvest when several lower leaves brown while upper leaves remain green; cure bulbs.

plants.name: Radishes
plants.growthForm: fast root crop with small leafy rosette
plants.regionalContext: Temperate United States with New England planning emphasis; local climate and cultivar selection take precedence.

soil.text: loose soil at least 6 in deep; deeper for daikon

spacingInches.text: 2 in for garden radishes; 4–6 in for large daikon

matureSizeInches.planningNote: Generalized planning range; cultivar and management can materially change mature dimensions.

timeToHarvest.text: garden radishes often 3–5 weeks; daikon longer

planting.directSow: Spring and late summer/fall; direct sow only.
planting.transplant: Not recommended.

plants.harvest: Pull promptly when roots reach usable size before becoming fibrous.

plants.name: Blueberries
plants.scientificName: Vaccinium spp. (highbush/half-high types common in home gardens)
plants.regionalContext: Temperate United States with New England planning emphasis; local climate and cultivar selection take precedence.
plants.frostTolerance: very hardy by cultivar; flowers can suffer spring frost

spacingInches.text: about 3 ft for compact northern types; larger cultivars require more

matureSizeInches.planningNote: Highbush and half-high blueberries vary strongly.

timeToHarvest.text: Meaningful harvests begin after 2–3 years; mature size/yield take longer.

planting.directSow: Not used for named cultivars.
planting.transplant: Plant nursery bushes in spring.

plants.harvest: Harvest fully blue ripe berries over repeated pickings.
plants.pollination: Plant two or more compatible varieties for better pollination/yield.

plants.name: Kale
plants.regionalContext: Temperate United States with New England planning emphasis; local climate and cultivar selection take precedence.

spacingInches.text: 12–18 in between plants

matureSizeInches.planningNote: Generalized planning range; cultivar and management can materially change mature dimensions.

planting.directSow: Spring or late summer.
planting.transplant: Spring and late summer.

plants.harvest: Harvest outer leaves continuously or cut whole plant; flavor often improves after cool weather.

plants.name: Mint
plants.regionalContext: Temperate United States with New England planning emphasis; local climate and cultivar selection take precedence.

spacingInches.text: 12–24 in initially; containment often recommended

matureSizeInches.planningNote: Can spread indefinitely without containment.

planting.directSow: Possible, but division/cuttings better preserve desired type.
planting.transplant: Plant divisions or nursery plants spring/fall.

plants.harvest: Cut stems/leaves throughout the season; frequent harvest encourages fresh shoots.
plants.support: Contain in pots/barriers if spread is undesirable.
plants.pollination: Flowers attract bees.

plants.name: Apples
plants.growthForm: fruit tree; size controlled strongly by rootstock
plants.regionalContext: Temperate United States with New England planning emphasis; local climate and cultivar selection take precedence.
plants.frostTolerance: cold hardy by cultivar/rootstock; flowers vulnerable to spring frost

spacingInches.text: Dwarf systems may space ~4–10 ft; semi-dwarf/standard trees need much more

matureSizeInches.planningNote: Rootstock and training system dominate mature dimensions.

planting.directSow: Seed does not reproduce cultivars true.
planting.transplant: Plant grafted nursery trees dormant/early spring.

plants.harvest: Harvest at cultivar-specific maturity using background color, seed color, flavor, and ease of separation.
plants.support: Stake dwarf trees as required by rootstock/training system.
plants.pollination: Most cultivars need a compatible pollinizer with overlapping bloom.

plants.name: Parsley
plants.growthForm: dense leafy basal clump; tall flower stalk second year
plants.regionalContext: Temperate United States with New England planning emphasis; local climate and cultivar selection take precedence.

spacingInches.text: 6–12 in depending on leaf type and harvest style

matureSizeInches.planningNote: Generalized planning range; cultivar and management can materially change mature dimensions.

timeToHarvest.text: often 70–90 days to mature leaf harvest

planting.directSow: Direct sow in cool soil; germination can be slow.
planting.transplant: Set seedlings out in cool weather.

plants.harvest: Harvest outer leaf stalks regularly while preserving the crown.
plants.pollination: Second-year flowers attract beneficial insects.

plants.name: Cilantro
plants.growthForm: open upright leafy herb that rapidly bolts
plants.regionalContext: Temperate United States with New England planning emphasis; local climate and cultivar selection take precedence.

spacingInches.text: 4–8 in for leaf harvest; can be denser for baby foliage

matureSizeInches.planningNote: Generalized planning range; cultivar and management can materially change mature dimensions.

timeToHarvest.text: leaf harvest often begins around 40–60 days; seed later

planting.directSow: Preferred in spring and succession sowings; also late summer/fall.
planting.transplant: Often not preferred because of taproot/bolting.

plants.harvest: Harvest leaves young; allow plants to flower/seed for coriander.
plants.pollination: Flowers support beneficial insects.

plants.name: Rosemary
plants.lifecycle: woody evergreen perennial; annual/container crop in cold climates
plants.regionalContext: Temperate United States with New England planning emphasis; local climate and cultivar selection take precedence.
plants.frostTolerance: frost sensitivity varies; often not reliably hardy in New England

spacingInches.text: 18–36 in depending on cultivar and pruning

matureSizeInches.planningNote: Generalized planning range; cultivar and management can materially change mature dimensions.

planting.directSow: Seed is slow; cuttings/plants are common.
planting.transplant: After frost; overwinter indoors where not hardy.

plants.harvest: Clip non-woody tips throughout the season; avoid severe cutting into old bare wood.
plants.pollination: Flowers attract bees.

plants.name: Thyme
plants.regionalContext: Temperate United States with New England planning emphasis; local climate and cultivar selection take precedence.
plants.frostTolerance: cold hardy by cultivar; winter wet is harmful

spacingInches.text: 12–18 in between plants

matureSizeInches.planningNote: Generalized planning range; cultivar and management can materially change mature dimensions.

planting.directSow: Possible but slow; transplants/divisions are common.
planting.transplant: After severe frost risk.

plants.harvest: Clip leafy stems before/through bloom; shear lightly after flowering.
plants.pollination: Flowers are highly attractive to bees.

plants.name: Raspberries
plants.lifecycle: perennial crown/root system with biennial canes
plants.regionalContext: Temperate United States with New England planning emphasis; local climate and cultivar selection take precedence.

spacingInches.text: often 2–3 ft between red raspberry plants; systems vary

matureSizeInches.planningNote: Generalized planning range; cultivar and management can materially change mature dimensions.

timeToHarvest.text: Cane fruiting begins after establishment; primocane vs floricane type matters.

planting.directSow: Not used for named cultivars.
planting.transplant: Plant dormant nursery stock in early spring.

plants.harvest: Pick fully colored berries that release easily; remove spent floricanes after harvest.
plants.pollination: Generally self-fruitful but bees improve fruit set.

plants.name: Winter Squash
plants.growthForm: very large ground-running vine with storage fruit
plants.regionalContext: Temperate United States with New England planning emphasis; local climate and cultivar selection take precedence.

spacingInches.text: 36–72 in depending on vine length

matureSizeInches.planningNote: Generalized planning range; cultivar and management can materially change mature dimensions.

planting.directSow: After frost once soil is warm.
planting.transplant: Young transplants after frost; avoid root disturbance.

plants.harvest: Harvest fully mature hard-rind fruit before hard frost; cure suitable types.
plants.pollination: Separate male/female flowers; insect pollination is important.

plants.name: Beets
plants.regionalContext: Temperate United States with New England planning emphasis; local climate and cultivar selection take precedence.

spacingInches.text: 3–4 in for mature roots

matureSizeInches.planningNote: Generalized planning range; cultivar and management can materially change mature dimensions.

planting.directSow: Spring and late summer.
planting.transplant: Possible when young.

plants.harvest: Harvest roots at desired size; greens are also edible.

plants.name: Dill
plants.regionalContext: Temperate United States with New England planning emphasis; local climate and cultivar selection take precedence.

spacingInches.text: thin to 10–12 in

matureSizeInches.planningNote: Generalized planning range; cultivar and management can materially change mature dimensions.

timeToHarvest.text: leaf harvest earlier; seed heads later

planting.directSow: Preferred after frost; succession sow every 2–3 weeks.
planting.transplant: Does not transplant easily.

plants.harvest: Harvest leaves as needed; collect mature seed heads when seeds brown.
plants.support: Tall plants may need wind protection/staking.
plants.pollination: Umbels attract many beneficial insects.

plants.name: Sage
plants.regionalContext: Temperate United States with New England planning emphasis; local climate and cultivar selection take precedence.
plants.frostTolerance: cold hardy by cultivar; dislikes wet crowns

spacingInches.text: 18–24 in between plants

matureSizeInches.planningNote: Generalized planning range; cultivar and management can materially change mature dimensions.

planting.directSow: Possible but slow; plants/cuttings common.
planting.transplant: After severe frost risk.

plants.harvest: Harvest leaves/shoot tips; prune lightly to maintain compact growth.
plants.pollination: Flowers attract bees.

plants.name: Swiss Chard
plants.growthForm: upright leafy plant with thick petioles
plants.regionalContext: Temperate United States with New England planning emphasis; local climate and cultivar selection take precedence.

spacingInches.text: 8–12 in between plants

matureSizeInches.planningNote: Generalized planning range; cultivar and management can materially change mature dimensions.

planting.directSow: Spring through midsummer.
planting.transplant: Spring or summer.

plants.harvest: Harvest outer leaves/stalks repeatedly while preserving center growth.

plants.name: Arugula
plants.regionalContext: Temperate United States with New England planning emphasis; local climate and cultivar selection take precedence.

spacingInches.text: 2–4 in for baby leaf; about 6 in for mature plants

matureSizeInches.planningNote: Generalized planning range; cultivar and management can materially change mature dimensions.

planting.directSow: Spring and late summer/fall; succession sow.
planting.transplant: Possible young but usually unnecessary.

plants.harvest: Harvest baby leaves or mature rosettes before heat-induced bolting.

plants.name: Garden Peony
plants.regionalContext: Temperate United States with New England planning emphasis; local climate and cultivar selection take precedence.

spacingInches.text: about 30–36 in

matureSizeInches.planningNote: Generalized planning range; cultivar and management can materially change mature dimensions.

planting.transplant: Plant divisions/bare roots in fall or early spring with eyes shallow.

plants.harvest: Remove spent flowers; allow foliage to persist until frost.
plants.support: Heavy double flowers may need rings/stakes.

plants.name: Black-eyed Susan
plants.regionalContext: Temperate United States with New England planning emphasis; local climate and cultivar selection take precedence.

matureSizeInches.planningNote: Generalized planning range; cultivar and management can materially change mature dimensions.

planting.directSow: Direct sow spring/fall; self-seeding common.
planting.transplant: Plugs can be planted spring/fall.

plants.harvest: Deadhead for tidiness or leave seedheads for wildlife.
plants.pollination: Strong native pollinator resource.

plants.name: Pears
plants.scientificName: Pyrus communis (European pear; other Pyrus types also grown)
plants.regionalContext: Temperate United States with New England planning emphasis; local climate and cultivar selection take precedence.
plants.frostTolerance: cold hardy by cultivar; flowers frost-sensitive

spacingInches.text: typically 10–20 ft depending rootstock/training

matureSizeInches.planningNote: Rootstock strongly controls tree size.

planting.transplant: Plant grafted nursery trees while dormant/early spring.

plants.harvest: Harvest mature pears before full tree-ripeness for many European cultivars; chill/ripen postharvest as appropriate.
plants.pollination: Many cultivars require or benefit from a compatible pollinizer.

plants.name: Plums
plants.regionalContext: Temperate United States with New England planning emphasis; local climate and cultivar selection take precedence.

spacingInches.text: traditional home-orchard spacing about 14 × 22 ft

matureSizeInches.planningNote: Generalized planning range; cultivar and management can materially change mature dimensions.

planting.transplant: Plant grafted nursery trees dormant/early spring.

plants.harvest: Harvest fully colored fruit when flesh develops cultivar softness/flavor.
plants.pollination: Pollination requirements vary; many Japanese plums require a compatible cultivar, while some European plums are self-fruitful.

plants.name: Sour Cherries
plants.regionalContext: Temperate United States with New England planning emphasis; local climate and cultivar selection take precedence.
plants.frostTolerance: winter hardy by cultivar; flowers vulnerable to spring frost

spacingInches.text: traditional red tart cherry spacing about 20 × 25 ft; dwarf rootstocks can be closer

matureSizeInches.planningNote: Generalized planning range; cultivar and management can materially change mature dimensions.

planting.transplant: Plant grafted nursery trees dormant/early spring.

plants.harvest: Harvest fully colored tart cherries; bird protection is often necessary.
plants.pollination: Many sour cherries are self-fruitful.

plants.name: Bok Choy
plants.regionalContext: Temperate United States with New England planning emphasis; local climate and cultivar selection take precedence.

spacingInches.text: 6–12 in depending on baby/full-size harvest

matureSizeInches.planningNote: Generalized planning range; cultivar and management can materially change mature dimensions.

planting.directSow: Spring or late summer.
planting.transplant: Best in cool weather.

plants.harvest: Harvest whole rosette or outer leaves before bolting.

plants.name: Collards
plants.regionalContext: Temperate United States with New England planning emphasis; local climate and cultivar selection take precedence.

spacingInches.text: 12–18 in for regular harvest; wider for full plants

matureSizeInches.planningNote: Generalized planning range; cultivar and management can materially change mature dimensions.

planting.directSow: Spring or late summer.
planting.transplant: Spring and late summer.

plants.harvest: Harvest outer leaves repeatedly; flavor improves in cool weather.

plants.name: Turnips
plants.regionalContext: Temperate United States with New England planning emphasis; local climate and cultivar selection take precedence.

spacingInches.text: 2–4 in for small roots; wider for large types

matureSizeInches.planningNote: Generalized planning range; cultivar and management can materially change mature dimensions.

planting.directSow: Spring and late summer.
planting.transplant: Not recommended for root quality.

plants.harvest: Harvest roots at desired size; greens are also edible.

plants.name: Butterfly Weed
plants.regionalContext: Temperate United States with New England planning emphasis; local climate and cultivar selection take precedence.

matureSizeInches.planningNote: Generalized planning range; cultivar and management can materially change mature dimensions.

planting.directSow: Seed benefits from cold stratification.
planting.transplant: Plant plugs young; deep taproot dislikes disturbance.

plants.harvest: Leave some pods/standing stems for habitat if desired.
plants.pollination: Important nectar plant and monarch host.
plants.toxicityNotes: Milky sap/plant tissues are toxic if eaten; sap can irritate.

plants.name: Wild Bergamot
plants.regionalContext: Temperate United States with New England planning emphasis; local climate and cultivar selection take precedence.

matureSizeInches.planningNote: Generalized planning range; cultivar and management can materially change mature dimensions.

planting.directSow: Can be seed-sown with cold stratification.
planting.transplant: Plant plugs/divisions spring or fall.

plants.harvest: Deadhead or leave seedheads; thin/divide spreading clumps as desired.
plants.pollination: Excellent bee, butterfly and hummingbird resource.

plants.name: Blazing Star
plants.regionalContext: Temperate United States with New England planning emphasis; local climate and cultivar selection take precedence.

matureSizeInches.planningNote: Generalized planning range; cultivar and management can materially change mature dimensions.

planting.directSow: Can be grown from seed; corms/divisions faster.
planting.transplant: Plant corms/plugs spring or fall.

plants.harvest: Leave some hollow stems for nesting bees; stake very tall stems if needed.
plants.pollination: Strong pollinator plant.

plants.name: Red Columbine
plants.growthForm: delicate basal mound with arching flower stalks
plants.regionalContext: Temperate United States with New England planning emphasis; local climate and cultivar selection take precedence.

matureSizeInches.planningNote: Generalized planning range; cultivar and management can materially change mature dimensions.

planting.directSow: Seed often benefits from cold stratification.
planting.transplant: Plant plugs in spring/fall.

plants.harvest: Allow some seed if naturalizing is desired.
plants.pollination: Early nectar source, especially for hummingbirds and long-tongued bees.

plants.name: Wild Geranium
plants.growthForm: mounded lobed foliage with flower stems
plants.regionalContext: Temperate United States with New England planning emphasis; local climate and cultivar selection take precedence.

matureSizeInches.planningNote: Generalized planning range; cultivar and management can materially change mature dimensions.

planting.directSow: Seed propagation possible; divisions are straightforward.
planting.transplant: Plant spring/fall.

plants.harvest: Shear declining foliage after spring bloom if needed.

plants.name: Blue Flag Iris
plants.regionalContext: Temperate United States with New England planning emphasis; local climate and cultivar selection take precedence.

soil.drainage: moist to wet; can tolerate shallow standing water

matureSizeInches.planningNote: Generalized planning range; cultivar and management can materially change mature dimensions.

planting.transplant: Plant/divide rhizomes in moist soil spring or late summer.

plants.harvest: Cut spent stalks if desired; divide overcrowded clumps.
plants.pollination: Native wetland flower used by pollinators.
plants.toxicityNotes: Rhizomes and other tissues can cause gastrointestinal irritation if eaten.

plants.name: Cardinal Flower
plants.regionalContext: Temperate United States with New England planning emphasis; local climate and cultivar selection take precedence.

matureSizeInches.planningNote: Generalized planning range; cultivar and management can materially change mature dimensions.

planting.directSow: Very fine seed; surface sow; cold treatment can aid germination.
planting.transplant: Plant plugs spring/fall in consistently moist soil.

plants.harvest: Allow basal rosettes/offsets to establish; avoid drying.
plants.pollination: Strong hummingbird and pollinator resource.

plants.name: Wild Blue Phlox
plants.regionalContext: Temperate United States with New England planning emphasis; local climate and cultivar selection take precedence.

matureSizeInches.planningNote: Generalized planning range; cultivar and management can materially change mature dimensions.

planting.transplant: Plant plugs/divisions spring/fall.

plants.harvest: Allow to form a loose woodland groundcover; trim after bloom if desired.
plants.pollination: Spring pollinator resource.

plants.name: Smooth Aster
plants.regionalContext: Temperate United States with New England planning emphasis; local climate and cultivar selection take precedence.

sprawling-cucurbit.description: Ground-running cucurbit vine with broad leaves and moderate-to-large fruit.

bulb-allium.description: Narrow upright leaves emerging from a basal bulb or pseudostem.

leafy-mound.description: Dense harvestable foliage forming a low or medium mound.

climbing-legume.label: Climbing legume

tuber-foliage.description: Above-ground foliage arising from an underground tuber or storage root system.

groundcover-stolon.description: Low perennial or spreading plant that propagates laterally by runners/stolons.

tall-grass.description: Strong vertical monocot form with long narrow leaves and elevated flowering/seed structure.

woody-shrub.label: Woody shrub

flower-stalk.label: Flower stalk
flower-stalk.description: Basal foliage or small crown with one or more conspicuous elevated floral stems.

broad-ornamental-shrub.label: Broad ornamental shrub
